full_judgment:
6. Leave has been granted to consider the submissions that the judgment of the High Court Division was not a proper judgment of  reversal and the High Court Division was wrong in holding that there was no presumption of correctness of RS Khatian under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and the observations in that behalf on the basis of which only the suit was decreed, were not at all correct and justified, that there having no consideration of the plaintiffs' case and the finding made by the trial Court against the plaintiffs, the decree passed in their favour is not legal and sustainable in law. 

 12. The learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that as in the RS Khatian No. 42 prepared under section 144 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 (the Act) names of sons of Durga Charan Mondal as well as Joy Gopal Mondal's son Ganesh Chandra Mondal appear and consequent thereupon as there is presumption of correctness of the entries in the said RS Khatian under section 144A of the Act, as such, treating the property of the said persons as vested property was quite legal. The presumption as regards the entries in the RS Khatian so attached under section 144A of the Act is rebuttable by leading evidence from the side of the person questioning correctness of the entry made therein. It is in the evidence of PW 1 that Durga Charan Mondal's sons having had fallen in distress some time in 1950 came to the house of Raj Chandra Mondal and Durga Charan Mandai's sons had no title in the land of Raj Chandra Mondal and Lechu Mondal and they stayed for some time but later on left the house of Raj Chandra Mondal. It is also in the evidence of PW 1 that names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons were wrongly recorded in the SA and RS Khatian. As against the aforesaid contention of PW 1 the evidence of DW 1 is that Ananda Mohan Mondal and others sons of Durga Charan Mondal were the SA recorded tenants and that they left for India at the time of war of 1965 and thereupon their land has been listed as vested property. This witness in cross-examination has stated that he cannot say on what basis names of sons of Durga Charan Mondal have been recorded in SA Khatian and that he cannot say Durga Charan Mondal's sons and Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal at what point of time went to India. Since from the materials on record it is seen that there was no. basis for recording names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and also name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal in the SA Khatian and also for making entries in the RS Khatian as regards address of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and. Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal shown as India has no basis, so the said entries in the RS Khatian were incorrect. Moreover, the Exhibit 6, Nadabi deed executed by Gonesh Chandra Mondal's son of Haripada Mondal reflects the fact of amicable partition of the property of Joy, Gopal Mondal between his, sons Kartik Mondal and Gonesh Chandra Mondal and thereupon Kartik Mondal got the property of Sarabo Mouza wherein the land in suit situates. It is seenfrom the materials on the, record that the entry in the RS Khatian as regards name of Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal reflecting interest in the land of Sarabo Mouza, wherein the land situates, is not correct. Since the presumption of correctness that has been attached to the RS Khatian by  the provision of section 144A of the Act has been rebutted and consequent thereupon recording of names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and Joy Gopal Mondal's son Gonesh Chandra Mondal was not correct, rather there was no basis for entering their names in the RS Khatian No. 42 and, as such, defendants (defendant Nos. 1 and 2) case of vested property on the basis of wrong entry of the names of persons having no title and interest in the land so listed in the RS Khatian in question has no leg to stand, rather the property in suit has been listed in the census list as vested property without ascertaining the correct position or without ascertaining particulars of the persons who have, in fact, right, title and interest in the land in suit. It appears the vested property authority has prepared the census list merely on the basis of wrongly prepared RS Khatian No. 42, and without ascertaining the real state of the matter is the property in suit in reality belongs to whom. 

 14. It is seen from the judgment of the High Court Division that the said Division: was of the view that RS record was prepared in terms of the provisions as are in Chapter IV of Part IV of the Act and thereupon expressed the view that presumption of correctness as to the entries in the SA and RS record finally published under section 19(3) in Chapter IV has no presumption of correctness. As against the said finding of the High Court Division the learned Counsel for the appellant has submitted that R'S record has been prepared as per provision of section 144 of Chapter XVII of part V of the Act and to the entries in the RS record so prepared under the said section of the Act presumption of correctness has been attached under section 144A of the Act. We have already held that presumption so attached under section 144A of the Act to the Khatians prepared under section 144 of the Act is rebuttable and the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 has rebutted the correctness of the entry made therein as regard the name of Durga Charan Mondal's sons and name or Gonesh Chandra Mondal son of Joy Gopal Mondal and, as such, the finding of the High Court Division that presumption of correctness as regard the entries in the RS Khatian is not available, is not correct, as submitted by the learned Counsel for the appellant, though of merit but for that the decision arrived at by the High Court Division that the property in suit is not vested property has not been materially affected since it has been established by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 that recording of the names of Durga Charan Mondal's sons as well as Gonesh Chandra Mondal, son of Joy Gopal Mondal in the SA and RS record of rights was not correct.
